title: X2 Turn requirements into work
subtitle: 09:40–10:15 · 35 minutes
description: Create two epics with six native sub-issues, one user story, and acceptance criteria from sourced requirements.
---

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- **Time:** 35 minutes
- **You produce:** three labels, two epics (E01, E08), six sub-issues with acceptance criteria, and one user story. You write one sub-issue yourself from a requirement. Each rule-based Issue names its source.
- **New terms:** [issue](../cheat-sheet.qmd#issue), [label](../cheat-sheet.qmd#label), [epic](../cheat-sheet.qmd#epic), [sub-issue](../cheat-sheet.qmd#sub-issue). All terms are in the [cheat sheet](../cheat-sheet.qmd).
:::

## Why this step

A thesis plan fails when it lists only intentions such as "write chapter 2". Work becomes manageable when each item names an **output**, an **owner**, **acceptance criteria**, and the **evidence** that shows completion. An Issue holds exactly these parts.

Two kinds of structure help. An **epic** groups the work for one substantial outcome, for example "Scope the thesis and register it". A **sub-issue** is one piece of that work with one output. GitHub links them natively: the epic shows the progress of its sub-issues. A **user story** states a need from the perspective of a person who will use the output: "As … I need … so that …". It reminds you that documentation has a reader.

Some work exists because a regulation requires it; other work is good practice. Mark the difference. A **Rule** Issue names its source, the article, and whether you verified it. Rules of this course (KSL) do not govern your thesis. The [requirements register](../../documentation/requirements.qmd) separates the two.

## Before you start

- You have the repository from [X1](x1.qmd).
- Find the titles and the bodies to copy in [Texts to copy](#texts-to-copy) at the end of this page.
- Open the [requirements register](../../documentation/requirements.qmd) in a third tab. You derive one Issue from it yourself.
- Command-line route: open a terminal in the folder `projm-thesis`.

## Steps

### Create the labels

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Click **Issues**, then **Labels**.
2. Click **New label**.
3. Type the name `kind:epic`, the description `Parent Issue for a substantial outcome`, and click **Create label**.
4. Repeat for `kind:task` (`Sub-issue with one output`) and `kind:story` (`Sub-issue written as a user story`).

#### Command line

1. Create the three labels:

   ```bash
   gh label create kind:epic --description "Parent Issue for a substantial outcome"
   gh label create kind:task --description "Sub-issue with one output"
   gh label create kind:story --description "Sub-issue written as a user story"
   ```

2. Check that the three labels exist:

   ```bash
   gh label list --search kind
   ```

:::

GitHub Issue Types exist only for organisations. Labels work in every personal account.

### Create the two epics

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Click **Issues**, then **New issue**.
2. Type the title `E01 Scope the thesis and register it`.
3. Paste the [body of E01](#text-e01).
4. On the right, click **Labels** and select `kind:epic`.
5. Click **Create**.
6. Repeat for `E08 Publish and preserve the outputs`.

#### Command line

Each command reads the body of one Issue in the [example repository](https://github.com/maehr/projm-example-thesis) and creates your Issue with this body. The bodies are the same as in [Texts to copy](#texts-to-copy).

1. Create the epic E01:

   ```bash
   gh issue view 1 -R maehr/projm-example-thesis --json body --jq .body \
     | gh issue create --title "E01 Scope the thesis and register it" --label kind:epic --body-file -
   ```

2. Create the epic E08:

   ```bash
   gh issue view 37 -R maehr/projm-example-thesis --json body --jq .body \
     | gh issue create --title "E08 Publish and preserve the outputs" --label kind:epic --body-file -
   ```

gh prints the address of each new Issue. The number at the end is the Issue number. In a new repository, E01 is `#1` and E08 is `#2`. The commands below use these numbers. If your numbers differ, use your numbers.

:::

### Derive one sub-issue yourself

Do not copy this one. Write it from the requirement, because that is what you will do for your real thesis.

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Open the epic E01. Below the description, click **Create sub-issue**. The button appears when the page has loaded.
2. Type the title `E01-T1 Check the registration requirements`.
3. Read requirement **R-05** in the requirements register and the sentence on page 5 of the [study plan](https://www.dh.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/fak_historisch/fsuf/d_dh/content/e1644823/e1776786/e1776810/e1777708/Studienplan_DH_Master_Major_Minor_ger.pdf) (Art. 15 Abs. 5).
4. Write the body in your own words. Use the five parts below.
5. Add the label `kind:task` and click **Create**.
6. Compare your Issue with [E01-T1 in the example repository](https://github.com/maehr/projm-example-thesis/issues/2). Add what you missed.

#### Command line

1. Read requirement **R-05** in the requirements register and the sentence on page 5 of the [study plan](https://www.dh.unibe.ch/unibe/portal/fak_historisch/fsuf/d_dh/content/e1644823/e1776786/e1776810/e1777708/Studienplan_DH_Master_Major_Minor_ger.pdf) (Art. 15 Abs. 5).
2. In a text editor, write the body in your own words. Use the five parts below.
3. Save the body as `e01-t1.md` in the folder that contains `projm-thesis`. Outside the repository, you cannot commit the file by mistake.
4. Create the sub-issue of E01 with this body:

   ```bash
   gh issue create --title "E01-T1 Check the registration requirements" --label kind:task \
     --parent 1 --body-file ../e01-t1.md
   ```

5. Compare your Issue with E01-T1 in the example repository:

   ```bash
   gh issue view 2 -R maehr/projm-example-thesis
   ```

6. Add what you missed to `e01-t1.md`. Then replace the body of your Issue. Use the number of your E01-T1:

   ```bash
   gh issue edit 3 --body-file ../e01-t1.md
   ```

:::

```markdown
**Output:** <what exists when the task is done?>
**Owner:** <who does it?>
**Basis:** Rule: <document, article, page> (<verified or unconfirmed>)

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] <a check that someone else can confirm>

**Evidence:** <what proves it, and where is it stored?>
```

### Create the other five sub-issues

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. In E01, click **Create sub-issue** again. Create `E01-T2` and `E01-T3` with the label `kind:task`. Copy the titles and the bodies from [Texts to copy](#texts-to-copy).
2. Open the epic E08. Create `E08-S1` with the label `kind:story`, then `E08-T2` and `E08-T3` with `kind:task`.

If you created an Issue on its own, open the epic, click the arrow next to **Create sub-issue**, and select **Add existing issue**.

{{< screenshot x2-epic-sub-issues >}}

#### Command line

1. Create the sub-issues E01-T2 and E01-T3 of E01 (`--parent 1`):

   ```bash
   gh issue view 3 -R maehr/projm-example-thesis --json body --jq .body \
     | gh issue create --title "E01-T2 Write the research question and scope" --label kind:task --parent 1 --body-file -
   gh issue view 4 -R maehr/projm-example-thesis --json body --jq .body \
     | gh issue create --title "E01-T3 Submit the thesis registration to the Dean's Office" --label kind:task --parent 1 --body-file -
   ```

2. Create the sub-issues E08-S1, E08-T2, and E08-T3 of E08 (`--parent 2`):

   ```bash
   gh issue view 38 -R maehr/projm-example-thesis --json body --jq .body \
     | gh issue create --title "E08-S1 Document the dataset for a future reuser" --label kind:story --parent 2 --body-file -
   gh issue view 39 -R maehr/projm-example-thesis --json body --jq .body \
     | gh issue create --title "E08-T2 Decide on rights and access for data and text" --label kind:task --parent 2 --body-file -
   gh issue view 40 -R maehr/projm-example-thesis --json body --jq .body \
     | gh issue create --title "E08-T3 Publish a demo release of the documented dataset" --label kind:task --parent 2 --body-file -
   ```

3. Check the epics. The line `sub-issues` lists three Issues for each epic:

   ```bash
   gh issue view 1
   gh issue view 2
   ```

If you created an Issue without `--parent`, add it to its epic afterwards. For example, `gh issue edit 1 --add-sub-issue 9` makes Issue 9 a sub-issue of E01.

:::

### Check one rule and one story

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Open `E01-T3`. Read the line **Basis**. Its status is *unconfirmed*: the regulation refers to dates that the Dean's Office publishes. Explain why the Issue does not invent a date.
2. Open `E08-S1`. Read the story. Name the person who needs the output.

{{< screenshot x2-task-blocked >}}

#### Command line

1. Show E01-T3. Read the line **Basis**. Its status is *unconfirmed*: the regulation refers to dates that the Dean's Office publishes. Explain why the Issue does not invent a date.

   ```bash
   gh issue view 5
   ```

2. Show E08-S1. Read the story. Name the person who needs the output.

   ```bash
   gh issue view 6
   ```

:::

## Texts to copy {#texts-to-copy}

Each text gives the title, the label, and the body of one Issue. The same Issues are in the [example repository](https://github.com/maehr/projm-example-thesis/issues?q=label%3Akind%3Aepic). E01-T1 is missing on purpose: you write it yourself.

{{< include _x2-texts.md >}}

## Expected state

- [ ] The labels `kind:epic`, `kind:task`, and `kind:story` exist.
- [ ] E01 shows three sub-issues; E08 shows three sub-issues.
- [ ] Each sub-issue has acceptance criteria as a checklist.
- [ ] E08-S1 has the label `kind:story` and the "As … I need … so that …" form.
- [ ] You wrote E01-T1 yourself; it names its source (SP-DH-2025 Art. 15 Abs. 5) and its status.
- [ ] E01-T3 names its source and the status *unconfirmed*.

## If something goes wrong

| Problem | Cause | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Create sub-issue** is missing. | The page shows a pull request, or an old layout. | Reload the Issue page. Use **Add existing issue** from the arrow next to the button. |
| A sub-issue is under the wrong epic. | — | Open the sub-issue. In the sidebar under **Relationships**, change the parent. |
| You created a "task list" in the epic text instead of sub-issues. | Checkboxes in text are not Issues. | Keep the text. Create real sub-issues as described. |
| You cannot create labels. | You are not the repository owner. | Ask the owner, or work as a collaborator with write access. |
| Time runs out. | — | Create E01 with its three sub-issues first. Add E08 in X3. |
| `gh issue create --parent` fails. | The number after `--parent` is not an epic in your repository. | Run `gh issue list --label kind:epic` and use the number of the epic. |
| A command fails. | Usually the installation, the sign-in, or the folder. | See [Command-line problems](../setup.qmd#command-line-problems), or do the step in the browser. |

## Alternatives

- **Pair:** one person creates E01 and its sub-issues, the other creates E08. Then review each other's acceptance criteria.
- **Private path:** the steps are the same. Rule sources stay public documents; the evidence (for example a transcript) belongs only in a private repository.
